nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 9:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Order Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Required Fields Present?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.email }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Abort — Malformed Input
nodes.notes: Fails fast with a clear message; triggers the error workflow instead of processing bad data. Watch out: Fails the run on purpose so the Error Workflow fires. This is intentional, not a bug.

nodes.name: Work in Batches
nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 10 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.name: Process Batch Item
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/orders — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Respect Rate Limits
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 seconds — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Aggregate Batch Results
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Mark Completed in Notion
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per order (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

# Recover incomplete checkouts: Google Sheets & Notion

**Pattern:** Abandoned Cart Recovery · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers inventory work end to end across Google Sheets, Notion, Slack and Discord.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)
3. Required Fields Present?
4. Abort — Malformed Input
5. Work in Batches
6. Process Batch Item
7. Respect Rate Limits
8. Aggregate Batch Results
9. Mark Completed in Notion
10. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
11. Archive Row Snapshot
12. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
13. Record Sub-workflow Result
14. Fingerprint for Idempotency
15. Drop Already-Processed Items
16. Stamp Completion Time
17. Persist Run Metadata
18. Load Previous Snapshot
19. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
20. Enrich with Reference Data
21. Fold In Enrichment Fields
22. Sort Orders Newest First
23. Save Execution Metadata
24. Stamp Processing Time
25. Guard Non-Empty email
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Notion)
28. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inventory work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets) → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Work in Batches → Process Batch Item → Respect Rate Limits → Aggregate Batch Results → Mark Completed in Notion → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Sort Orders Newest First → Save Execution Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty email → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Notion aligned by hand for inventory
- Inventory sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Google Sheets
- A backlog too large to push into Google Sheets in one pass, across 31 nodes
- Inventory work where "Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Notion in step for inventory, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Notion are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this inventory build
- A failed Google Sheets or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this inventory build
- Bad input stops the run for inventory instead of landing in Google Sheets
- The pause before Google Sheets is durable — a inventory run survives a restart

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The batch size and the Wait between iterations exist specifically to respect the downstream API's rate limit — processing everything as fast as possible just gets the workflow throttled or banned. Marking items completed only after a batch succeeds leaves a clean resume point if the run dies mid-way, instead of an ambiguous half-processed state.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Lower the batch size and raise the wait — measure the throughput/reliability tradeoff directly.
2. Simulate a failed item mid-batch and see exactly what 'Mark Completed' captures.
3. Point the queue read at a different store platform.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inventory process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
inventory payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
